name: GitHub
description: A direct registration path, with an important app-type decision.
verdict: Start by choosing OAuth App or GitHub App. Registering an app and gaining access to customer resources are separate steps.
estimateBasis: Planning estimate for initial configuration only; excludes implementation and customer policy decisions.

scopes.name: read:user
scopes.purpose: Read profile information; confirm the endpoints your feature needs.

steps.title: Choose your OAuth identity
steps.detail: Use managed auth if its current permissions fit. For your own app, compare GitHub Apps: fine-grained permissions and installation control may suit repository access better.
steps.done: Record the selected app type and why it serves your feature.

steps.title: Prepare registration details
steps.detail: Have a public application name, homepage and callback URL ready. If using Composio, copy the redirect URI from the custom auth configuration; do not guess it.
steps.done: The homepage and exact callback URL are recorded.

steps.title: Register the OAuth app
steps.detail: Open GitHub Settings → Developer settings → OAuth apps → New OAuth App. Fill in the application details and callback URL. Keep generated secrets in your secret manager or Composio.
steps.done: A provider registration exists, with credentials kept outside this guide.

steps.title: Request only the necessary scopes
steps.detail: Map your feature to specific API endpoints and their scopes. A repository integration may be better served by GitHub App permissions.
steps.done: Each requested permission has an endpoint and feature justification.

steps.title: Authorize one test account
steps.detail: Complete the authorization flow in your own integration or Composio and make a harmless read request. Record only the status and redacted result. Account authorization is distinct from app registration.
steps.done: The intended test resource can be read with the granted permissions.

sources.title: Composio · managed vs custom auth
sources.excerpt: Composio manages OAuth apps for GitHub, Gmail and Slack. Custom credentials support your own consent identity and scope needs.

sources.title: GitHub · creating an OAuth app
sources.excerpt: The registration flow asks for an application name, homepage and callback URL. GitHub recommends considering a GitHub App.

sources.title: GitHub · OAuth scopes
sources.excerpt: Scopes limit token access. Request only the permissions required for the endpoints your integration calls.

sources.title: GitHub · authorizing OAuth apps
sources.excerpt: Web applications redirect users to authorize the app, then exchange the returned code for a token.

blockers.title: The wrong app type for repository access
blockers.detail: An OAuth App acts on behalf of a user. Compare the finer-grained permissions of GitHub Apps before committing to this model.
blockers.action: List required repository actions and compare the documented app types.

blockers.title: Callback configuration does not match
blockers.detail: Use the provider’s redirect rules and the callback supplied by the integration platform.
blockers.action: Compare the registered callback with the actual authorization request; never paste a client secret into this report.

unknowns: Customer organization access policies need account-specific checking.
The full OAuth exchange has not been executed for this guide.
tested: Official documentation reviewed. Custom registration entry redirected to sign-in; no custom app was registered. Separately, a Composio-managed GitHub OAuth connection completed after owner consent: server status ACTIVE and read-only GET /user returned HTTP 200 on 29 October 2026. No provider approval is claimed.

name: Slack
description: Workspace setup is quick. Distribution needs a separate decision.
verdict: Separate an internal workspace app, a customer pilot and Marketplace distribution. Check eligibility before preparing a submission.
estimateBasis: Planning estimate for configuration and preparation; excludes building the app, pilot usage and review.

scopes.name: chat:write
scopes.purpose: Post messages where the app has the necessary access.
scopes.classification: Bot scope; validate against your endpoints

steps.title: Choose the distribution path
steps.detail: Choose a single-workspace app, a limited pilot, or broader distribution. Composio-managed OAuth may cover your prototype; confirm the capabilities and customer policies.
steps.done: Audience and OAuth identity are documented.

steps.title: Create a Slack app
steps.detail: Open the Slack app dashboard and associate the app with a development workspace. Confirm that your account may create and install apps.
steps.done: The app exists in an authorized development workspace.

steps.title: Configure permissions and redirects
steps.detail: Add only the needed bot/user scopes and configure the exact redirect URI. Wider distribution requires an OAuth installation flow and HTTPS URLs.
steps.done: Permissions map to features and the redirect configuration is saved.

steps.title: Install and test in your workspace
steps.detail: Install the app, complete the required authorization and run a harmless test. Respect workspace installation policies.
steps.done: A test interaction works in the intended workspace.

steps.title: Check Marketplace eligibility before submission
steps.detail: Review current eligibility, including at least 10 active workspaces and 10 weekly active users, and meaningful in-Slack functionality. A product offering only an MCP server without meaningful Slack functionality is listed as unsuitable.
steps.done: Eligibility and preparation gaps are recorded; submission is a separate action.

sources.title: Composio · managed vs custom auth
sources.excerpt: Composio manages OAuth apps for GitHub, Gmail and Slack. Custom credentials support your own consent identity and scope needs.

sources.title: Slack · app lifecycle and distribution
sources.excerpt: Single-workspace apps, unlisted pilots and Marketplace distribution have different installation paths. Workspaces may require admin approval.

sources.title: Slack · Marketplace requirements
sources.excerpt: Marketplace suitability includes usage and functional requirements. MCP-only offerings without meaningful functionality inside Slack are listed as unsuitable.

sources.title: Slack · installing with OAuth
sources.excerpt: Configure scopes and redirects for an OAuth installation flow; keep bot and user permissions distinct.

blockers.title: Marketplace eligibility comes before submission
blockers.detail: A working OAuth flow alone does not establish suitability for Marketplace listing.
blockers.action: Check intended functionality and current active-usage criteria before investing in submission materials.

blockers.title: Workspace administrator approval
blockers.detail: Some workspaces restrict app installation or allow only Marketplace-listed apps.
blockers.action: Ask a workspace administrator to confirm the installation policy and approve the required access.

unknowns: Your target workspace policy has not been inspected.
Marketplace acceptance and elapsed review time cannot be predicted.
tested: Official distribution and Marketplace guidance reviewed. Creation dialog and name/workspace form inspected; blocked by workspace sign-in. No app created or installed.

name: Gmail
description: The permissions you choose can change the entire approval path.
verdict: Inbox-reading access uses restricted scopes. For external production use, investigate verification and the data-handling assessment requirements early.
estimateBasis: Planning estimate for basic configuration and collecting requirements; excludes security remediation, assessment and provider review.

scopes.name: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send
scopes.purpose: Send messages on behalf of the user.

steps.title: Choose managed auth or your own project
steps.detail: Check Composio-managed OAuth scope coverage. If using your own identity, choose the exact capabilities, intended audience and data handling before registering credentials.
steps.done: OAuth identity, audience and features are explicit.

steps.title: Prepare your app identity and public pages
steps.detail: Prepare your application homepage, support details and required privacy disclosures. For applicable verification, establish domain ownership. Public pages must describe the real product and its actual data practices.
steps.done: Required public URLs and domain-verification responsibilities are identified.

steps.title: Configure the project and OAuth client
steps.detail: Use the Google Cloud Console to enable the relevant API, configure branding/audience/data access and register the web client. Use the exact redirect URI supplied by your integration.
steps.done: The project, client and redirect are configured; secrets stay in the provider or secret manager.

steps.title: Justify the minimum scopes
steps.detail: Send-only uses gmail.send, a sensitive scope. Inbox reading uses gmail.readonly, a restricted scope. Keep the feature, endpoint and scope mapping together.
steps.done: Every scope has a genuine feature justification.

steps.title: Test with an eligible account
steps.detail: Follow the development/testing rules and complete one test connection. Testing can have user and token-lifetime limitations; it does not establish production verification.
steps.done: A permitted test account authorizes and the intended harmless operation succeeds.

steps.title: Assess restricted-data handling
steps.detail: Determine whether restricted data passes through or is stored on your servers. Review security-assessment applicability and exceptions; do not assume an assessment is unnecessary.
steps.done: The applicable assessment path or unresolved question is documented.

steps.title: Prepare the applicable verification submission
steps.detail: Review exceptions first. For applicable external production access, collect accurate branding, ownership, scope justifications and demonstration materials. Google makes the verification decision.
steps.done: Required materials are prepared; actual submission and provider outcome are recorded separately.

sources.title: Composio · managed vs custom auth
sources.excerpt: Composio manages OAuth apps for GitHub, Gmail and Slack. Custom credentials support your own consent identity and scope needs.

sources.title: Google · Gmail API scopes
sources.excerpt: gmail.send is sensitive; gmail.readonly is restricted. Server storage or transmission of restricted-scope data introduces assessment requirements.

sources.title: Google · restricted scope verification
sources.excerpt: Verification preparation includes application identity, domain ownership and public policy information. Exceptions and development/testing limitations are documented separately.

sources.title: Google · OAuth production policies
sources.excerpt: Production readiness includes accurate identity, minimal scopes and applicable sensitive/restricted-scope verification.

blockers.title: Restricted-data assessment
blockers.detail: Data handling affects assessment requirements. A working test connection does not remove production obligations.
blockers.action: Document the data flow and check the applicable restricted-scope assessment requirements and exceptions.

blockers.title: Public identity and ownership are incomplete
blockers.detail: Verification preparation includes public app information and applicable domain ownership checks.
blockers.action: Prepare accurate public pages, then confirm ownership in the provider console.

unknowns: The developer’s data flow and exception eligibility need confirmation.
No verification decision, assessment cost or review duration has been established.
tested: Official scope classifications and production-readiness requirements reviewed. No project, OAuth exchange or approval submitted.
